svg.text: Option C (preferred): Passport as the identity home, backend in Homegate
Sign-in as in A.1. The Homegate is picked on the sign-in screen. Passport manages profiles with a child grant.
Already have a pubky? Import it
Grant only, key loaded to sign
1 Log in, with the chosen Passport
you pick a Homegate or enter an invite code
4 wrapping key (and sign-up code if new)
key kept in browser, or loaded only to sign
signs up on the code's homeserver
5 signed parent grant (or from Ring or Bitkit)
8 redirect back with a child grant
9 Log in, like any suite app
10 child grant: Passport edits the profile
+ Apps only link Passport. Users can pick their own Passport instance in the
+ No lock-in: each identity picks its Homegate, or a homeserver with no
+ An invite code works too: the code picks its homeserver.
+ Profile management works for every identity, also when the key is in Ring or
+ Users choose how much the browser holds: the key, or only a grant.
+ One site handles keys and SSO sign-in.
− Homegate must derive Passport's current wrapping key, or existing backups
− Each Homegate needs its own SSO setup (Google client, Apple Services ID).
− Sign-in options depend on the chosen Homegate, so the screen differs per
− SSO backup needs a Homegate. Own homeserver without one: import or Mobile
− Backups are bound to the Passport address that made them. Another instance
needs a recovery file or a change.
− Moving an SSO identity to another Homegate means re-encrypting its backup.
Passport can do it in its UI.
− Grant-only SSO identities need an SSO sign-in each time Passport has to sign.
− The SDK needs a setting for the Passport address.
